When the flood of sound has dissolved, when the manifestation of the *bindu* has subsequently ceased, and when that reality—which is inseparable from the eightfold resonance (*aṣṭadhvani*)—has been attained;
On the occasion of the Śakti-parvan, the yogi relishes his own self-awareness—
known as the Blessed Goddess Śivā— which is unfathomable as pure consciousness and is of the nature of supreme bliss,
whose body is the infinite sovereignty of Śiva, and which is formless. (18)

May you alone— whose nature is wisdom, whose compassion is boundless, who gives birth to the worlds, and who is the abode of the unsurpassed state— be the goal for those who worship you, whether it be worldly existence or liberation. 19.

Having placed the universe within his body, he places that within his heart; he places that within the Puruṣa, and the Puruṣa within the Bindu; he places that within the profound space known as Viyat; he places all this within that which is called Jñāna;
and he places even that within the profound depth of supreme bliss, in the form of the Great Void—thus victorious is he whose nature is the experience of You.
O Ordainer! O Knowable One! O Knowledge! O Thou of diverse traditions!

O thou who art like a garland of the Vedas! O Wondrous One! O Primordial of the universe! O thou who art easily attained through discipline! O Mother of the Vedas! O Knower of Śiva! O thou who dwellest on the trident! O thou who bestowest the state of Śiva! O Treasure of Śiva! O Auspicious One! O Mother! Grant [this] to me through thee!
Incomparable devotion. || 21 ||
O Mother! That Giriśa took Viṣṇu’s severed head and made it a vessel in his palm;
that he placed Hari, impaled upon his trident, as an ornament upon his shoulder;
and that he adorned his neck with the poison—all this belongs to you, the Śakti who abides in Śiva.
The playfulness. || 22 ||
O Mother! Known as Viriñci, you create; known as Hari, you protect the three worlds;
known as Rudra, you destroy; and assuming the state of Īśvara, you ordain sovereignty. Becoming Nāda, you sport as the shatterer of the flood of bonds; you alone are the one who becomes many.
O Daughter of the Mountain, by means of various ritual acts. || 23 ||
O Mother! It is impossible for the minds of the sages— even when their passions are somewhat gladdened— to ever touch it, as they remain perpetually trembling with awe.
O Pārvatī, how do the summits of the Vedas, so naturally hard, find their place upon your most tender sprout-like feet? 24.

They describe her as the eternal flash of lightning, the river of nectar free from banks, the moonlight transcending all impurity, the primordial nature devoid of the thicket of the knots of the *guṇas*, the knowledge beyond words, the Mother of the Universe with unbowed breasts, and the boundless Lakṣmī.
The virtuous [praise] the Blessed One. || 25 ||

The body is composed solely of insentient matter such as earth, water, and so forth; yet this conscious person experiences pleasure and pain. O Daughter of the Mountain, even though he clearly knows this, the embodied soul is unable to abandon the ego-identification with the body, for he stands outside Your teaching.

When my father, mother, brother, friend, follower, home, wife, body, field, companion, and even wealth abandon me, then, O Great Moonlight! O Mother! by your compassion, become for me that which instantly shatters the blinding darkness of fear and delusion.
The one who brings about accumulation. || 27 ||

O Mother of the Universe! It is said that you were first born as the daughter of Dakṣa; thereafter, having abandoned him who was possessed of faults, you became the daughter of the King of Mountains. Though you are the beginningless and endless Śakti, non-different from Śambhu, yet—alas! who can comprehend your wondrous life-story—that through marriage you became his wife?

The sun, the moon, fire, and other luminaries are but particles of Your radiance; the Supreme Brahman is merely a tiny drop of Your bliss. From Śiva down to the earth, everything within Your three-fold body dwells in Your belly; yet You manifest wondrously in the heart of Your devotee—how marvelous!
O Blessed One! || 29 ||
Before and behind, within and without, immeasurable and measured, supreme, gross and subtle, with parts and without parts, secret and non-secret.
O Blessed One, you always bear the name known as Paśyantī, which gives rise to the agitation of the worlds, perceiving the entire universe as "far," "near," "existent," and "non-existent."

Having entered your path through innate compassion and the vision of the Teacher, [I perceive] my own self as the body of Śiva— possessing a mercy that transcends counting, which cuts through the mass of darkness on the six paths, which instantly bestows auspiciousness, and which carries out the supreme command.
Blessed are those who for a long time obtain the Blessed Lady.
O Mother! As rays arise from the sun, as sparks from a fire,

as waves from the ocean, and as droplets from a force whose majesty is checked— so do the multitudes of principles arise again and again within You through Your own sattvic qualities, attaining tranquility at every moment.
They are under the control of others. || 32 ||
Vidhi, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Prakṛti, the Aṇu, the Ātman, Dinakara, Svabhāva, Jaina, Sugata-muni, Ākāśa, Malina, Śiva, and Śakti—
by these conceptual constructs, the wise bring You within the range of the Vedas and thus designate You.
To the Blessed Lady. || 33 ||

You are Śiva; you are Śakti; you are the vow (samaya); you are the observer of the vow (samayinī); you are the Self; you are initiation; you are this entire collection of qualities such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest; you are ignorance; you are knowledge;
you are everything—what else could there be, O Blessed One? No separate reality exists apart from you.
We two shall look upon them.
O Mother! He knows through you, he creates through you alone, and he desires through you constantly;
you are indeed all his bodies. Though you bear the likeness of the entire universe of Śambhu, whose form is the supreme sky, you nevertheless sport as half of Śiva.
What is this? || 35 ||
O Mother! After countless previous births, at the conclusion of a single birth through the dissolution of karma, one attains Giriśa in the form of a Guru.
Having obtained the Śaiva command, I have come to know even you, whose body is Śiva;
I shall pass my days solely by composing hymns and worship for you.
That which is the arisen six-petaled lotus, its center known as the *karṇikā*,
within the womb of which is celebrated the seat of the syllable *Oṃ*; and within that [seat] is she who is bent by the weight of her breasts,
renowned as Kuṇḍalinī, dark-hued, the Mother of all beings— [meditate on her] constantly.
I meditate. || 37 ||

On earth, in water, in fire, in wind, in space, in the moon, in the sun, and even in the sacrificer—your single power is eightfold. O Mother of all beings, you who bear the entire universe even while bent low by the weight of your breasts: may you, who are beyond description, protect me.
Thus ends the *Pañcastavī*, and the fifth [chapter], the hymn to the Mother of All Beings (*Sakalajananīstava*).
